findings.title: Item-resume flow is correct and observable end to end
findings.description: The full D8 path holds up under inspection: lock → state/`report.json` validation (`_check_record` enforces flagged/not_run and accept-only-for-`review_unresolved`) → git precondition (`restore_target` from a flagged slice branch, clean-target check, `verify_git_state`) → item re-selection (reconcile-to-PASSED when merged-but-unreported, rejection naming the status otherwise) → dependency re-check → body run. Every failure mode maps to a distinct `ResumeExit` code, is logged at the right level (`WARNING` for rejections, `ERROR` for HALTED), and the tests assert both the code and the log signal (`test_an_unknown_git_state_mid_item_halts`, `test_a_failed_report_rewrite_halts_and_keeps_the_old_report`). The `typer.Exit → HALTED` translation in `handle_item_resume` for mid-item classification/auth refusal is coherent, and the `GitEnvironmentError` re-raise in `_run_pipeline_sdk` when `item_rerun` is set correctly leaves report writing to the `each` step's `finally`. No action needed.

findings.title: Run lock only guards commit/branch-moving pipelines, but "mutates" hazards include plain review and fan_out runs
findings.description:
`pipeline_mutates` counts only `design/tasks/implement/devlog/branch` steps (plus `loop` with `commit_each_iteration`). But the module's own docstring justifies the lock by "interleave" and "race on `report.json`" — and both hazards also arise from pipelines that never commit:
- A standalone `review:` step (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:_save_part`) writes `project-documents/user/reviews/{slice}-review.{template}…md` into the working tree. Two concurrent runs of the same slice (e.g. `judge-cycle`, which starts with a top-level review step) race on that file, and each run's review reads the other run's inputs mid-mutation.
- `fan_out` step configs use `inner:`/`models:` keys, not `steps:`, so `_step_mutates` never sees their dispatch bodies — a fan-out pipeline whose branches write files is classified as non-mutating.

All *shipped* pipelines happen to be covered (each contains a phase/branch step; `P6`/`implement`/`P456`/`P56` via `branch`, `slices-plan`/`tasks-plan` via `design`/`tasks`, `implement-plan` via the `each` body), which is why the parametrized test passes — but the detection is a narrower property than the docstring's claimed one, and any project-local pipeline shaped like `judge-cycle` slips through un-locked. Either widen the detection (review writes, `fan_out.inner`) or narrow the docstring to "one committing/branch-moving run per checkout" and document the residual file-level race.

findings.title: resume_item's blanket OSError handler mislabels unrelated I/O faults as report-write failures
findings.description: `except OSError as exc: return ResumeOutcome(HALTED, f"cannot write the batch report: {exc}")` is justified by the comment for the report-write failure mode, but the same clause also catches OS errors raised anywhere else in `_resume_locked` — e.g. `evaluate_each_source` → `_design_dependencies`/`_review_flag` do `read_frontmatter` on design/review files in the checkout (see `src/squadron/pipeline/sources.py:_design_dependencies`, which explicitly anticipates `OSError` per file and demotes it to a warning, and `_cf_slices_ready_to_implement`'s dependency reads, which do not). An unreadable design file there would surface to the operator as "cannot write the batch report" — an active write failure that didn't happen. Narrow the clause to the two actual write call sites (`_reconcile`, the `_open_dependencies` branch) or wrap `report.write` explicitly so the message stays truthful.

findings.title: Checkpoint override instructions stored in run state silently apply to the entire resumed run
findings.description: A checkpoint ACCEPT/OVERRIDE merges `OVERRIDE_INSTRUCTIONS` into `merged_params`, and the state callback persists `dict(params)` (including it) to the run file. On `--resume` (`run.py` resume path → `_run_pipeline_sdk(dict(state.params))`) or implicit paused-run resume, that instruction is re-injected into every dispatch for the rest of the run — even the ones in *other* items of an `each` step. That contradicts the design the diff itself enforces for item resume: `item_params` deliberately *drops* stored reserved keys with a WARNING ("an earlier run's instructions never carry into a decision", `src/squadron/pipeline/item_resume.py:item_params`). The asymmetry is at least plausible (checkpoint instructions were meant for "the rest of this run"), but it's currently undocumented anywhere the operator can see it, and `item_params`' reserved-key drop shows the authors thought about exactly this once. Decide whether stored `override_instructions` should also be dropped (or logged) on plain resume, or documented.

findings.title: No load test accompanies the new per-item report rewrite
findings.description: `_execute_each_step` now rewrites `report.md` + `report.json` (each via `asyncio.to_thread`, so off-loop) after *every* item (`await _write_each_report(report, runs_dir, final=False)`), doubling the file writes on the batch path plus the per-item `StateManager` load. `tests/load/` exists and gates concurrency-adjacent paths, but this slice adds no load entry for, say, a 100-item plan asserting rewrite latency stays within bounds. Cheap to add later; flagging for the test-with convention.

findings.title: Item-resume forces the SDK execution path regardless of the stored run's mode
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` builds a `run_body` that always calls `_run_pipeline_sdk`, but plain `--resume` honors `state.execution_mode` (SDK vs PROMPT_ONLY, `run.py`). A `PROMPT_ONLY` batch run resumed with `--item` will classify for an SDK session and raise `typer.Exit(1)` inside Claude Code, which the handler reports as "Item did not finish (exit 1)". The path is rejected loudly (not silently) and prompt-only batches are an edge, but the mode was available at the call site in `run()` if you ever want to honor it.
